We buy as-is. Tell us about the property and the timeline.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from Oklahoma statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

Oklahoma property tax is assessed and collected at the local level, and owners can appeal an assessment. Here is what the official sources say.

What the official sources say

  • If the assessor increases real property value, the taxpayer has 30 calendar days from the notice mailing date to file a written protest with the county assessor. (68 O.S. § 2876(E); source)
  • A protest where the valuation did not change may be filed on or before the first Monday in April. (68 O.S. § 2876(F); source)
  • The assessor issues a written decision within 7 calendar days of the informal hearing; the taxpayer then has 15 calendar days from mailing of the decision to appeal to the county board of equalization. (68 O.S. § 2876(H); source)
  • The taxpayer must file the Section 2835 form with the protest; if not filed, a presumption favors the assessor's valuation in any appeal. (68 O.S. § 2876(G); source)
  • Appeal from the county board of equalization goes to district court (Court of Tax Review if fair cash value exceeds $3,000,000); notice of appeal is due within 30 calendar days of the board order being mailed; trial is de novo. (68 O.S. § 2880.1(A)-(B); source)
  • Full taxes must be paid when due during an appeal; a pending appeal abates and is dismissed if taxes are delinquent and unpaid. (68 O.S. § 2884(A); source)
  • Statewide assessment level for locally valued property is a minimum of 11% and maximum of 13.5% for each real property subclass (10%-15% for personal property). (2024 Ad Valorem Statistics Book, Oklahoma Tax Commission; source)
  • Assessor and board of equalization proceedings and appeals are the sole method to correct assessments or abate taxes. (68 O.S. § 2885(A); source)
  • Real estate with taxes unpaid three years or more is advertised and sold at the county resale held the second Monday of June each year. (68 O.S. § 3105(A); source)
  • A county may run the resale as an online auction beginning within the week of the second Monday of June. (68 O.S. § 3125; source)
Selling in Oklahoma?

How to sell a Oklahoma house when this applies to you

  1. Find out what the title company needs. For an inherited or transferred house, that usually means the recorded deed or the probate paperwork that shows who owns it today.
  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See we buy houses in Oklahoma.

What a cash sale of a Oklahoma house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Oklahoma.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.
  3. Pick your closing date. You choose the timeline. Some owners need weeks to move out, and others want to close quickly.
  4. The title company handles the paperwork. It checks ownership, pays off any mortgage and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds, and records the deed.
  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

Documents and information to have ready

You do not need everything below to get an offer, but each item makes the sale smoother and helps the title company work faster.

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing, selling it yourself or a cash offer: how they compare

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required Oklahoma disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

Questions to ask before you sell in Oklahoma

  • Ask the title company what is owed and what the title company will need at closing.
  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.
  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

These are general questions to start a conversation, not legal advice. Rules in Oklahoma change, so confirm details with the official office or a Oklahoma attorney or tax professional.

More questions about selling in Oklahoma

How fast can I close on a cash sale?

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

Do I have to clean out or repair the house?

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Will you buy a house that has tenants in it?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

No. Requesting an offer is free and carries no obligation.

  • An additional $1,000 assessed-valuation exemption applies for heads of households whose gross household income for the preceding calendar year did not exceed $30,000. (68 O.S. § 2890; source)
  • The exemption is granted for a tax year only if the application is filed with the county assessor by March 15 (or within 30 days after a valuation increase notice, whichever is later); later applications take effect the following tax year. (68 O.S. § 2892(A); source)
  • A taxpayer granted a homestead exemption who continues to occupy the home as a homestead need not reapply. (68 O.S. § 2892(C); source)
  • Homestead means the actual residence of a natural person who is a citizen of this state and holds record ownership; only one homestead exemption in the state is allowed per person or family. (68 O.S. § 2888(A)(1); source)
  • Application for the limit on fair cash value of a homestead (Art. X, Sec. 8C) is due by March 15 or within 30 days after a valuation increase notice, whichever is later; no annual reapplication once qualified. (68 O.S. § 2890.1(A)-(B); source)

title: Oklahoma Eviction Process and Selling a Rented House
content:
Oklahoma Eviction Process and Selling a Rented House

Cash Home Buyers in Oklahoma
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Inherited, behind on payments, tenants, repairs: we buy it as-is
  • Zero fees, zero commissions, zero closing costs
  • No obligation: turn the offer down and owe us nothing

Selling a Oklahoma House? Get a Cash Offer

We buy as-is. Tell us about the property and the timeline.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from Oklahoma statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

Oklahoma evictions follow notice and court steps set by state law. Here is what the official sources say.

What the official sources say

  • A landlord may terminate for nonpayment if rent is not paid within 5 days after written demand; the demand is deemed a demand for possession. (41 O.S. § 131(B); source)
  • For a material lease breach, the landlord gives written notice terminating the lease not less than 15 days after receipt unless remedied within 10 days. (41 O.S. § 132(B); source)
  • Month-to-month and at-will tenancies are terminated by 30 days' written notice from either party; tenancies shorter than month-to-month need 7 days. (41 O.S. § 111(A)-(B); source)
  • Notice is served personally, otherwise on a family member over 12, otherwise by posting plus certified or first-class mailing. (41 O.S. § 111(E); source)
  • District court has jurisdiction over forcible entry and detainer; rent and damages claims may be joined. (12 O.S. § 1148.1; source)
  • Summons sets trial not less than 5 nor more than 10 days from issuance and must be served at least 3 days before trial. (12 O.S. §§ 1148.4-1148.5; source)
  • On judgment for the plaintiff a writ of execution issues to the sheriff; a new-trial motion must be filed within 3 days and does not stay execution. (12 O.S. § 1148.10; source)
  • A landlord's conveyance of real estate is valid without the tenant's attornment; rent paid to the grantor before written notice of the conveyance is good against the grantee. (41 O.S. § 119(A); source)
  • On sale, the owner is relieved of liability for events after written notice to the resident; the successor is liable for all obligations under the rental agreement and the resident pays rent to the successor after notice. (41 O.S. § 119(C); source)
  • Under the OREC form, all leases are assigned to the Buyer at closing, security deposits transferred and prepaid rent prorated. (OREC 2026 Residential Sale contract form, Para. 11C; source)
  • A fixed-term tenancy expires on its ending date without notice unless earlier terminated. (41 O.S. § 111(C); source)

Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from Oklahoma statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

This guide covers what official sources say about Oklahoma transfer on death deeds. Here is what the official sources say.

What the official sources say

  • An interest in real estate may be titled in transfer-on-death form by a recorded deed signed by the record owner naming grantee beneficiaries; no consideration is required. (58 O.S. § 1252(A); source)
  • No beneficiary signature, consent or notice is needed during the owner's lifetime. (58 O.S. § 1252(B); source)
  • The deed must be executed, acknowledged and recorded with the county clerk where the land lies before the owner's death. (58 O.S. § 1253; source)
  • After death, each accepting beneficiary records an affidavit with the death certificate within nine months or the interest reverts to the decedent's estate (deaths on or after Nov. 1, 2011). (58 O.S. § 1252(D)-(E); source)
  • The designation may be revoked or changed before death by a recorded instrument or later TOD deed; a will cannot revoke a recorded TOD deed. (58 O.S. § 1254; source)
  • Beneficiaries take subject to recorded mortgages, liens and other interests; if a beneficiary dies first, that transfer lapses. (58 O.S. § 1255; source)
  • A TOD deed is not a testamentary disposition and cannot be invalidated for nonconformity with Titles 58 or 84. (58 O.S. § 1258; source)
  • Summary administration may be petitioned if the estate is $300,000 or less, the decedent has been dead more than five years, or the decedent resided in another jurisdiction. (58 O.S. § 245(A); source)
  • A summary administration order has the effect of a final decree and a certified copy or notice must be recorded with the county clerk where the decedent held real property. (58 O.S. § 247(B); source)
  • A successor affidavit procedure allows delivery of tangible personal property and debts to a successor 10 or more days after death if the estate does not exceed $50,000 and no personal representative has been appointed. (58 O.S. § 393(A); source)

  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.

  4. The title company handles the paperwork. It checks ownership, pays off any mortgage and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds, and records the deed.
  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

Documents and information to have ready

You do not need everything below to get an offer, but each item makes the sale smoother and helps the title company work faster.

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing, selling it yourself or a cash offer: how they compare

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required Oklahoma disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.
  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Cash Offer in 24 Hours

Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from Oklahoma statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

This guide covers Oklahoma foreclosure sales according to official sources. Here is what the official sources say.

What the official sources say

  • On levy against land, three disinterested persons (or an impartial legal entity) appraise the property and return a signed estimate of real value. (12 O.S. § 759(B); source)
  • Property may not be sold for less than two-thirds of the appraised value returned. (12 O.S. § 762; source)
  • Notice of sale is mailed first-class at least 10 days before sale to the debtor and interest holders, and published for two successive weeks in a county newspaper. (12 O.S. § 764(A); source)
  • The sale may not be held less than 30 days after first publication; a bidder other than the execution party may be required to post 10% in cash or certified funds within 24 hours. (12 O.S. § 764(C); source)
  • The sheriff may elect to conduct the sale through an online auction marketplace. (12 O.S. § 764(D); source)
  • The sale is confirmed by the court after notice of hearing mailed at least 10 days before; no buyer's premium may be charged; the court then orders the sheriff's deed. (12 O.S. § 765; source)
  • The sheriff's deed conveys the estate the judgment debtor could have conveyed and must be executed, acknowledged and recorded. (12 O.S. § 766; source)
  • The court may issue a writ of assistance to put the purchaser in possession on confirmation. (12 O.S. § 686; source)
  • Real estate securing a debt may be sold only under a court judgment ordering the sale (judicial foreclosure). (12 O.S. § 686; source)
  • A deficiency requires a motion within 90 days after sale (or with the motion to confirm); the court sets fair market value; if no motion is made, sale proceeds are deemed full satisfaction. (12 O.S. § 686; source)
  • If 'appraisement waived' appears in the mortgage, no order of sale issues until six months after the initial judgment. (12 O.S. § 760; source)
  • Non-judicial foreclosure is allowed under the Power of Sale Mortgage Foreclosure Act if the mortgage contains the statutory bold, underlined power-of-sale statement. (46 O.S. § 43(A); source)
  • Before power-of-sale foreclosure, the mortgagee must send notice of intent by certified mail giving 35 days from the date sent to cure. (46 O.S. § 44; source)
  • Notice of sale must be personally served at least 30 days before sale and published weekly for four consecutive weeks, first publication at least 30 days before sale. (46 O.S. § 45(B); source)
  • A homestead mortgagor may elect judicial foreclosure by certified-mail notice to the mortgagee and recording a copy at least 10 days before the power-of-sale date. (46 O.S. § 43(A)(2)(b); source)
  • The mortgagor may redeem up to completion of the sale by paying the amount owed and expenses; the power-of-sale deed is absolute without right of redemption (except a federal statutory right). (46 O.S. §§ 43(B), 47(B); source)
